<!-- pr-reviewer: 612a5d896f830a6556834877a1b130a38f2ef5f4 -->
Read, not built - needs a maintainer look (touches `.github/workflows/release.yml` and adds the script `web/check-app-page.sh`). One blocker: the front page claims a browser build even when the wasm job failed.

**Blocker**
1. `site/templates/index.html:21`: "The browser build is CamCraft {{ version }}, built from the same release tag as this site" prints whenever `version` is set. Zola builds the site before the wasm result is known, so when the wasm job fails the front page still says a build exists and links to the "not part of this copy" page. The issue asks that the page say what it is. Fix: state only what is certain (for example, "A release carries the browser build when its run built it; if the link shows a page saying it is not part of this copy, the browser build failed for that release"), or pass the wasm result into the site build and choose the sentence from it.

**Checked and good**
- Triggers: the `on:` block (release.yml:27-30) is unchanged: `push: tags: ['v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.0']` and `workflow_dispatch`. No new trigger.
- `wasm` job (release.yml:451-486): `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`; job-level `permissions: contents: read` (453-454); no secrets. Its `uses:` lines are `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, the same major-tag style as the rest of the file.
- Downloads and pins:
  - `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` (release.yml:463): rustup on the runner, no version or checksum. A component install, not a script download. Acceptable, but unpinned.
  - `apt-get install clang-18 llvm-18` (465): pinned to a major version through the Ubuntu archive (signed, no checksum).
  - WASI sysroot `wasi-sysroot-34.0` from the wasi-sdk release (web/build-app-wasm.sh:42-44): pinned by version and sha256 `9d813544…a2be`, checked at lines 62-63.
  - wasm-bindgen-cli (build-app-wasm.sh:128-146): version read from the tools lock file, installed with `cargo install --version … --locked`. Pinned by version and lock, crates.io, no checksum.
  - `cargo fetch --locked` (build-app-wasm.sh:72).
  - No `curl | sh` in the diff.
- Failure isolation:
  - `site`: `needs: [wasm]` and `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` (release.yml:495-496).
  - The download runs only `if: needs.wasm.result == 'success'` (531-534). The else branch (548-550) names the missing build with `::warning::` and checks that the fallback `app/index.html` is non-empty.
  - `publish` (286-287) and `pages` (556-562) conditions are unchanged. `pages` still needs `site` and `publish` to succeed and runs only on a tag.
- Artifact flow: `wasm` uploads `wasm-app` from `target/web/` only (482-486, `if-no-files-found: error`). `site` downloads it after `zola build` (530) and before `upload-pages-artifact` (552). Nothing else from the wasm checkout is uploaded or packaged, which answers #949.
- Fallback collision: on success, `rm -rf site/public/app` (545) runs before the copy (546), so the browser build replaces Zola's `app/index.html`. The fallback page never reaches the artifact.
- `web/check-app-page.sh`: `set -euo pipefail` (line 18); variables quoted; takes the folder as its argument; checks the four files are non-empty and the `.wasm` magic number; rejects `src=`/`href=`/`action=`, import-map values, `import`/`from`, `fetch(`, and `new URL`/`Worker` values that start with `/` or `http(s):`; rejects `SharedArrayBuffer`. No network access. LF endings (no CR). Git mode 100755.
  - Note: the `http(s):` rule also rejects an absolute https link in the shell's own HTML. Fine today; a future shell that links its own docs that way would fail the wasm job.
- Site links: the front page uses `get_url(path='@/app.md')` and the first-run guide uses `@/app.md`, so the links follow the base URL and a fork's Pages works. The templates are ours; the text names the version and what does not work (the #31 list).
- Decision file, `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1103` are present in the PR body and commit.

**The three cases**
- wasm succeeds: `site/public/app/` is replaced by the browser build (545-547), the check runs on the copy, and the docs and the release go out. `pages` deploys `app/`.
- wasm fails: the download is skipped, the warning names the result (549), Zola's stand-in stays at `app/`, and `test -s` passes (550). `pages` still gets `site` and `publish`, so the docs go out. The front page still says a build exists (the blocker).
- `workflow_dispatch`: `wasm` builds and uploads `wasm-app` (no deploy); `site` builds its copy; `pages` and `publish` are tag-only (287, 562), so nothing is deployed.

**Non-blocking notes**
- release.yml:547 runs `check-app-page.sh` a second time on the site copy. The wasm job already ran it on the same files at line 475. If this second run fails, `site` fails and withholds `pages`, which the issue says a failed browser build must not do. Consider dropping it or making it a warning there.
- release.yml:550: the fallback check `test -s` makes the stand-in page load-bearing; if `content/app.md` is ever removed, the docs job fails.
- `site/templates/index.html` says "it runs on a thread, and the browser gives the shell none": jargon. The issue asks for plain English.
- The estimate of 12-18 billed Linux minutes per cut is the author's, not measured.

**Only a real tag run can prove**
- The Linux tool installs (clang-18/llvm-18, the `CC_`/`AR_` variables), the wasm-bindgen-cli build on Linux, the copy and check on the runner, the Pages deploy, and whether `/Camcraft/app/` loads in Chrome and Firefox. The author's notes say the same.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1e345767467ea6af86c63c6cdf29d5b7bc4d4d36 -->
Read, not built - needs a maintainer look. Re-check of head 1e345767 (read-only). The earlier blocker (front page claims a browser build) is closed, and the two notes are addressed. No blockers remain.

**The author's own change:** one commit, `1e345767`, since 612a5d89, touching `release.yml` (the `site` job), `site/templates/index.html`, `base.html`, `app.md`, `first-run.md`, `site/README.md` and the decision file. Everything else in the branch diff comes from the merge of main, and `git merge-tree` of origin/main with the head is clean.

**(1) Blocker closed.** Every page that mentions the browser build reads the `app` flag:
- `base.html:4-5` sets `app` true only when `version.toml` has `app = true`.
- `index.html:19-25`: "Open CamCraft X in your browser" only when `version and app`; with a version but no flag, "not available"; with no version (local preview), "comes with a released copy".
- `app.md` says the build is not part of this copy and names the failure case; `first-run.md` says "When this site's release has a browser version". Neither claims a build.

**(2) The `site` job, line by line** (`set -e` is active in this `shell: bash` step):
- Flag step 541: `elif ! bash web/check-app-page.sh /tmp/wasm-app; then` is inside an `if`, so a failed check cannot kill the step. Line 546 writes `app = true|false`.
- Build step 560-561: `build()` runs zola and `test -s public/index.html`. The first `build` (561) runs with the flag as set.
- Copy 563: `if ! { rm -rf site/public/app && cp -r ... && check; }`. A failing check inside `if !` is caught, not fatal.
- Flip 565 `sed -i 's/^app = true$/app = false/'` matches the line written at 546, then `build` at 566 rebuilds after the flip. The rebuild does happen.
- `test -s site/public/app/index.html` (569) runs in every case.

Three cases:
- **wasm ok:** download (521-525) succeeds; flag true; copy and check pass; no rebuild; upload (570) runs.
- **wasm failed:** download skipped (524); flag false with the warning (541 is not reached, the `!= success` branch warns); no copy; zola's fallback at `app/` stays; `test -s` passes; upload runs.
- **check fails on the copy:** flag true; the copy check fails; `app/` is removed, the flag flipped to false, the site rebuilt, warning raised; upload runs.

**Requested (small, not blocking):** in the copy-failed branch, `rm -rf site/public/app` is not explicit before the rebuild at 566. The half copy is removed only if zola's `build` clears `public/` itself. Add `rm -rf site/public/app` before `build` so the result does not depend on zola's behaviour.

**(3) Unchanged:** the `on:` block (27-30) is the same, with only the tag push and `workflow_dispatch`. The `wasm` job (445-487) and its permissions (453-454) are unchanged; the pins (rustup, apt clang-18/llvm-18, the WASI sysroot sha256 and wasm-bindgen `--locked`) are unchanged. `publish` (287) and `pages` (574-580) are unchanged; the diff from 612a5d89 touches only lines 518-572.

**(4) Mergeable:** GitHub still says `UNKNOWN` after a re-read; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main FETCH_HEAD` exits 0 with no conflicts.

**(5)** `web/check-app-page.sh`: mode 100755 and no CR, as before.

**Only a real tag run can prove:** the Linux tool installs, the copy and check on the runner, the rebuild and flag flip path, and the Pages deploy.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
